activity.notes: Muwatalli II (also commonly spelled Muwattalli II in scholarly publications) was a Great King of the Hittite Empire and one of the principal rulers of its imperial period. He transferred the royal seat from Hattusa to Tarhuntassa, maintained and strengthened Hittite control in western Anatolia and Syria, concluded the treaty with Alaksandu of Wilusa, and commanded the Hittite forces against Ramesses II at the Battle of Kadesh in 1274 BCE. ATLAS uses c. 1295-1272 BCE as the representative reign chronology following Trevor Bryce's modern reconstruction. Both boundaries are approximate because Hittite absolute chronology remains reconstructed and other references retain differing endpoints, including c. 1295-1282 BCE. The user-supplied label Hittite is normalized to the imperial-period map polity Hittite Empire.

sources.title: The Showdown with Egypt: The Reign of Muwattalli II (c.1295–1272) — The Kingdom of the Hittites
sources.citation_text: Trevor Bryce dates Muwattalli II's reign approximately 1295-1272 BCE and treats the transfer of the Hittite seat to Tarhuntassa, the Syrian conflict with Egypt, and the Battle of Kadesh as central events of his reign.

sources.title: Treaty between Muwattalli II of Hatti and Alaksandu of Wilusa — British Museum 108569
sources.citation_text: The British Museum catalogs a Hittite treaty between Muwattalli II, king of Hatti, and Alaksandu of Wilusa, providing direct material evidence for his sovereign authority and western Anatolian diplomacy.

sources.title: The Hittites — The Metropolitan Museum of Art
sources.citation_text: The Metropolitan Museum describes Muwatalli's transfer of the capital to Tarhuntasha, continued Hittite control in western Anatolia, the Alaksandu treaty, and the confrontation with Ramesses II at Kadesh. Its differing reign dates illustrate the need to mark ATLAS year boundaries approximate.
